subject: Film & Cinema
title: Soviet Montage: Editing as Revolution
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Soviet Montage: Editing as Revolution.

hook.text: The Soviet government saw cinema as the perfect propaganda tool — and funded it.

buildup.text: Eisenstein, Vertov, and Pudovkin believed editing was cinema's most powerful weapon.

discovery.text: The Kuleshov Effect proved that the same face, cut with different images, changes meaning.

twist.text: Their experiments were political tools, but the techniques transcended ideology.

climax.text: Every film editor today uses principles these Soviet filmmakers discovered.

punchline.text: Propaganda funded film's deepest artistic discoveries.

quiz.question: What does the Kuleshov Effect demonstrate?
options: Editing context changes how we interpret an image
